name: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021
description: Personal data processing under the ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated August 2025): what a data processing agreement and the processing it governs must meet in the ADGM. English is the language of ADGM legislation. DRAFT: not yet legally reviewed.

clauses.title: Principles relating to Processing of Personal Data: principles
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Principles relating to Processing of Personal Data: accountability
clauses.content: The Controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate compliance with, section 4(1).
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Lawfulness of Processing: lawful bases
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processing of Special Categories of Personal Data: special categories
clauses.content:
Processing of:
(a) Personal Data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs;
(b) Genetic Data, Biometric Data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, Data Concerning Health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation; and
(c) Personal Data relating to criminal convictions and offences or related security measures, (together, ‘Special Categories of Personal Data’) is prohibited.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Responsibility of the Controller: controller’s measures
clauses.content:
Taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of Processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for the rights of natural persons, the Controller must:
(a) implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and to be able to demonstrate that Processing is performed in accordance with these Regulations; and
(b) review and update those measures where necessary.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Joint Controllers: joint controller arrangement
clauses.content: Where two or more Controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of Processing, they are joint Controllers. They must determine their respective responsibilities for compliance with the obligations under these Regulations in a transparent manner, in particular as regards the exercising of the rights of the Data Subject and their respective duties to provide the information referred to in sections 11 and 12, by means of an arrangement between them unless the respective responsibilities of the Controllers are determined by Applicable Law. The arrangement may designate a contact point for Data Subjects.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processor: processors with sufficient guarantees
clauses.content: Where Processing is to be carried out on behalf of a Controller, the Controller must use only Processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures in such a manner that Processing will meet the requirements of these Regulations and ensure the protection of the rights of the Data Subject.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processor: sub-processors need written authorisation
clauses.content: The Processor must not engage another Processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the Controller. In the case of general written authorisation, the Processor must inform the Controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of other Processors, thereby giving the Controller the opportunity to object to such changes.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processor: what the contract must contain
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)
clauses.guidance: The contract must set out the subject-matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, the types of personal data and data subjects, and the controller’s rights and obligations; and bind the processor to documented instructions, confidentiality, security (s. 30), sub-processor conditions, assistance with data subject rights and ss. 30–34, deletion or return at the end, and information and audits.

clauses.title: Processor: notice of infringing instructions
clauses.content: With regard to section 26(3)(a), the Processor must immediately inform the Controller if, in its opinion, an instruction contravenes these Regulations or other data protection provisions contained in Applicable Law.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processor: sub-processors bound by the same obligations
clauses.content: Where a Processor engages another Processor for carrying out specific Processing activities on behalf of the Controller, the same data protection obligations as set out in the contract or other legal act between the Controller and the Processor as referred to in section 26(3) must also be imposed on that other Processor by way of a contract or other legal act under Applicable Law, in particular, providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures in such a manner that the Processing will meet the requirements of these Regulations. The initial Processor remains fully liable to the Controller for the performance of that other Processor's obligations.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processor: contract in writing
clauses.content: The contract or the other legal act referred to in sections 26(3) and 26(5) must be in writing.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Processing under the authority of the Controller or Processor
clauses.content: The Processor and any person acting under the authority of the Controller or of the Processor, who has access to Personal Data, must not Process that data except on instructions from the Controller, unless required to do so by Applicable Law.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Records of Processing activities: processor’s records
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Security of Processing: security measures
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Notification of a Personal Data Breach to the Commissioner of Data Protection: controller notifies within 72 hours
clauses.content: In the case of a Personal Data Breach, the Controller must without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the Personal Data Breach to the Commissioner of Data Protection, unless the Personal Data Breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights of natural persons. Where the notification to the Commissioner of Data Protection is not made within 72 hours, it must be accompanied by reasons for the delay.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Notification of a Personal Data Breach to the Commissioner of Data Protection: processor notifies the controller
clauses.content: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Communication of a Personal Data Breach to the Data Subject: communication to data subjects
clauses.content: When the Personal Data Breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights of natural persons, the Controller must communicate the Personal Data Breach to the Data Subject without undue delay.
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: General principle for transfers: conditions for any transfer
clauses.content: Any transfer of Personal Data that is undergoing Processing or is intended for Processing after transfer to a jurisdiction outside of ADGM or to an International Organisation can only take place if, subject to the other provisions of these Regulations, the conditions in this Part are complied with by the Controller and Processor, including for further onward transfers of Personal Data.
clauses.section: Part V: Transfers of Personal Data outside of ADGM or to International Organisations
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision: adequacy
clauses.content: A transfer of Personal Data outside of ADGM or to an International Organisation may take place where the Commissioner of Data Protection has decided that the receiving jurisdiction, one or more specified sectors within that jurisdiction, or the International Organisation in question ensures an adequate level of protection of Personal Data. Such a transfer will not require any specific authorisation.
clauses.section: Part V: Transfers of Personal Data outside of ADGM or to International Organisations
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)

clauses.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards: appropriate safeguards
clauses.content: In the absence of a decision pursuant to sections 41(3) or 41(7), a Controller or Processor may transfer Personal Data to a Controller or Processor outside of ADGM or to an International Organisation only if the Controller or Processor has provided appropriate safeguards, and on condition that enforceable Data Subject rights and effective legal remedies for Data Subjects are available.
clauses.section: Part V: Transfers of Personal Data outside of ADGM or to International Organisations
clauses.source_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (consolidated version August 2025, ADGM Rulebook)
